title: Nine thousand open flow mappings followed by 140,608 lines of distinct keys
notes: The input is never closed, so it is an error: a syntax error at the end of the input, or a limit error if the reader refuses the nesting first. No result is allowed. The keys of the innermost mapping are 140,608 different names (`xaaa` to `xZZZ`, none of them a number, boolean or null), so a reader that rejects duplicate keys still reads every line. A reader that looks at every open flow mapping for each line does about 1.3 billion steps here and goes over the bound. The bound is on total time, so a reader that is only slow per line can miss it too; it does not by itself show that the cost grows with depth (see safety/shallow-flow-mappings-then-many-lines-unclosed, the same lines at depth 100). The time bound is the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. Input: nine thousand `{`, then each name followed by a comma and a line break.

provenance.reference: A reader whose time was quadratic here: each line was checked against the pending implicit-key slot of every open flow mapping, taking nine seconds for a five megabyte input of this shape.
